title: The Economics Of Wildfires And Heatwaves In Europe
gist: Gavekal's Cedric Gemehl frames the unprecedented French and Spanish wildfires and the latest southern European heatwave as negative supply shocks, but argues wildfires specifically have limited macro impact because they are geographically and temporally concentrated, partly recoverable, and followed by stimulative reconstruction and government support. Heatwaves are presented as operating through a different transmission channel, which the teaser does not disclose.

themes.theme: Climate events as supply shocks in the European macro outlook

insights.claim: Wildfires and heatwaves should both be analysed in economic terms as negative supply shocks, but they transmit into the economy through different channels and therefore should not be modelled as one climate variable.
insights.speaker: Cedric Gemehl
insights.so_what: Do not lump climate disruptions into a single 'weather' adjustment when forecasting European growth and inflation; separate the discrete capital-destruction shock from the ongoing productivity/energy-demand shock.
insights.quote: In economic terms, both wildfires and heatwaves can be understood as negative supply shocks. Their economic effects, however, operate through different channels.
insights.locator: In economic terms, both wildfires and heatwaves

insights.claim: France and Spain are racing to combat wildfires burning on an unprecedented scale at the same time as another heatwave sweeps across southern Europe.
insights.speaker: Cedric Gemehl
insights.so_what: A simultaneous fire-and-heat shock in two large euro area economies is a live input to Q3 European activity data, insurance loss estimates and regional tourism revenue.
insights.quote: With France and Spain racing to combat wildfires that are raging on an unprecedented scale just as another heatwave sweeps across southern Europe

insights.claim: It is worth asking explicitly whether climate-related events can materially move a developed-market macro outlook at all, rather than assuming headline severity translates into economic significance.
insights.speaker: Cedric Gemehl
insights.so_what: Frames the trade: dramatic climate headlines may be a fade for macro positioning if the transmission channels are shallow.
insights.quote: it pays to ask whether climate-related events can materially affect the European macro outlook

themes.theme: Why wildfire damage stays local rather than macro

insights.claim: Wildfires destroy physical capital and inflict severe human costs, yet their impact on aggregate output tends to be limited, because fires are concentrated in geography and time, some lost output is recovered once the fire is contained, and reconstruction spending plus government support stimulate activity afterwards.
insights.speaker: Cedric Gemehl
insights.so_what: Argues against marking down euro area GDP forecasts on fire headlines; the post-event fiscal and rebuild impulse can even net out positive for construction and materials exposure.
insights.quote: Their impact on aggregate output, however, tends to be limited for three main reasons.

insights.claim: Reconstruction spending and government support after a wildfire tend to stimulate activity, so the fiscal response is part of the shock's economic profile and not merely a transfer.
insights.speaker: Cedric Gemehl
insights.so_what: Monitor French and Spanish emergency and reconstruction budget lines as a small pro-cyclical fiscal impulse rather than a drag.
insights.quote: Third, reconstruction spending and government support tend to stimulate activity after the shock.
